Definition: from a prolonged form of G4894; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness:--conscience.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the Gentiles show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness, with thoughts accusing or excusing one another, and he warns that sinning against a brother wounds his weak conscience, and that is sin against Christ. The end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned, and the blood of Christ purges the conscience from dead works to serve the living God. A good conscience is not a feeling but a cleansed witness, and Peter says to keep it so that accusers are ashamed.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe conscience is God's witness inside me, accusing and excusing, and I hold that only the blood of Christ can purge it clean. I take the warning seriously: wounding a brother's conscience is sin against Christ Himself, so I will guard both my conscience and his.
